question: Under § 12-10-101(1), "Director" means:
choice_a: The director of the division of real estate
choice_b: The director of the Department of Regulatory Agencies
choice_c: The chairperson of the real estate commission
choice_d: The executive director of the division of professions and occupations
explanation: Section 12-10-101(1) defines 'Director' to mean the director of the division of real estate.

question: Section 12-10-101 defines exactly three terms: Director, Division, and HOA. Which commonly-used term in this article is NOT defined there, because it is instead defined separately in § 12-10-201(1)?
choice_a: Division
choice_b: Commission
choice_c: Director
choice_d: HOA
explanation: "Commission" is not one of the three terms defined in § 12-10-101; it is defined separately in § 12-10-201(1) as the real estate commission created in section 12-10-206.

question: Under § 12-10-201(1), the term "Commission" means:
choice_a: The division of real estate
choice_b: A percentage-based fee paid to a broker
choice_c: The real estate commission created in section 12-10-206
choice_d: The Colorado Real Estate Guaranty Fund board
explanation: Section 12-10-201(1) defines 'Commission' to mean the real estate commission created in section 12-10-206, distinguishing the regulatory body from the compensation meaning of the word used elsewhere in the article.

question: Under § 12-10-206, the five-member real estate commission appointed by the governor must be composed of:
choice_a: Five licensed real estate brokers with no minimum experience requirement
choice_b: Two real estate brokers and three public representatives
choice_c: Four real estate attorneys and one public representative
choice_d: Three real estate brokers with at least five years of Colorado experience (at least one with substantial property management experience) and two public representatives
explanation: Section 12-10-206 requires the commission to consist of three real estate brokers with at least five years of Colorado experience, at least one of whom has substantial property management experience, plus two public representatives.

question: Under § 12-10-206, real estate commission members serve terms of how many years, and for what reasons may the governor remove a member before the term ends?
choice_a: Three-year terms; removal for misconduct, neglect of duty, or incompetence
choice_b: Two-year terms; removal only for a felony conviction
choice_c: Six-year terms; members may not be removed before term expiration
choice_d: Four-year terms; removal requires a unanimous commission vote
explanation: Section 12-10-206 sets three-year terms for commission members and authorizes the governor to remove a member for misconduct, neglect of duty, or incompetence.

question: Under § 12-10-206, the real estate commission is organized within Colorado's administrative structure as a:
choice_a: Type 2 entity
choice_b: Type 1 entity
choice_c: Freestanding independent agency outside DORA
choice_d: Division-level board with rulemaking authority delegated to the director
explanation: Section 12-10-206 designates the real estate commission as a type 1 entity, funded through the Division of Real Estate cash fund, for purposes of Colorado's administrative organization scheme.

question: Under § 12-10-201(3), the term "limited liability company" as used in part 2 of article 10:
choice_a: Is defined independently within part 2, without cross-reference to other titles
choice_b: Excludes single-member LLCs from broker licensure
choice_c: Has the same meaning as set forth in section 7-80-102(7)
choice_d: Is limited to LLCs organized exclusively for real estate brokerage
explanation: Section 12-10-201(3) does not create a freestanding definition; it incorporates by cross-reference the meaning given to 'limited liability company' in section 7-80-102(7).

question: Under § 12-10-201(5), the term "partnership" as used in part 2 of article 10 includes:
choice_a: Only general partnerships formed under Colorado law
choice_b: Joint ventures that have not filed formation documents
choice_c: Any unincorporated business association regardless of registration
choice_d: A registered limited liability partnership
explanation: Section 12-10-201(5) states that 'partnership' includes a registered limited liability partnership.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(a)(I), which act, when done for compensation, is a core enumerated activity making a person a 'real estate broker'?
choice_a: Selling, exchanging, buying, renting, or leasing real estate or an interest therein
choice_b: Preparing a comparative market analysis for a for-sale-by-owner seller at no charge
choice_c: Appraising real property for a mortgage lender
choice_d: Serving as a court-appointed receiver managing rental property
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(a)(I) enumerates selling, exchanging, buying, renting, or leasing real estate, or an interest therein or improvements affixed thereon, as an act constituting broker activity when done for compensation.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(a)(III), which activity is specifically enumerated as broker activity when performed for compensation?
choice_a: Drafting a residential lease for a landlord who is a personal friend, without a fee
choice_b: Selling or offering to sell or exchange an existing lease of real estate or an interest therein
choice_c: Notarizing a lease document
choice_d: Collecting rent as an unpaid family member helping a relative
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(a)(III) enumerates selling or offering to sell or exchange an existing lease of real estate, or an interest therein or improvements affixed thereon, as broker activity.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(a)(IV), which act is enumerated as broker activity distinct from merely selling or listing property?
choice_a: Reviewing a title commitment as a licensed title insurance producer
choice_b: Providing a home inspection report
choice_c: Negotiating the purchase, sale, or exchange of real estate or an interest therein
choice_d: Recording a deed with the county clerk
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(a)(IV) enumerates negotiating the purchase, sale, or exchange of real estate, or an interest therein or improvements affixed thereon, as broker activity.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(a)(V), which act, done for compensation, is enumerated as making a person a 'real estate broker'?
choice_a: Filing a plat with the county assessor
choice_b: Advertising one's own home for sale without engaging a broker
choice_c: Serving as a public trustee in a foreclosure sale
choice_d: Listing, offering, attempting, or agreeing to list real estate for sale, exchange, rent, or lease
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(a)(V) enumerates listing, offering, attempting, or agreeing to list real estate, or an interest therein or improvements affixed thereon, for sale, exchange, rent, or lease.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(a)(VII), a person who buys, sells, or otherwise deals in options on real estate for compensation, or acts as an 'option dealer,' is engaged in:
choice_a: An enumerated act constituting 'real estate broker' activity
choice_b: An activity exempted under § 12-10-201(6)(b)
choice_c: Conduct regulated only under 4 CCR 725-1, not the statute
choice_d: An activity that requires a separate 'option dealer' license distinct from a broker license
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(a)(VII) lists dealing in options on real estate, or acting as an 'option dealer,' as one of the enumerated acts that constitutes 'real estate broker' activity when done for compensation.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(a)(VIII), a salaried employee who performs the enumerated broker acts on behalf of the owner of real estate, at a salary or for a fee or commission, is:
choice_a: Automatically exempt because the owner directs the employee's work
choice_b: Engaged in an enumerated act constituting 'real estate broker' activity
choice_c: Exempt so long as the employee's title is 'property manager'
choice_d: Exempt if the salary is less than 75 percent of total compensation
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(a)(VIII) enumerates performing the foregoing acts as an employee of, or on behalf of, the owner of real estate at a salary or for a fee, commission, or other consideration as broker activity. This is distinct from the narrower corporate-officer exemption in § 12-10-201(6)(b)(VIII), which requires at least 75 percent of compensation from salary.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(I), an attorney-in-fact acting under a power of attorney duly executed by an owner of real estate is exempt from the 'real estate broker' definition only if the attorney-in-fact acts:
choice_a: With compensation not exceeding a customary commission
choice_b: With the written approval of the real estate commission
choice_c: Without compensation
choice_d: Within thirty days of the power of attorney's execution
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(I) exempts an attorney-in-fact acting WITHOUT compensation under a duly executed power of attorney authorizing consummation of a real estate transaction. Compensated attorneys-in-fact do not qualify for this exemption.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(II), which person is exempt from the 'real estate broker' definition when engaged in real-estate-related activity?
choice_a: Any licensed insurance agent handling a title insurance claim
choice_b: Any elected county assessor performing a private property sale
choice_c: Any notary public witnessing a deed
choice_d: Any public official in the conduct of official duties
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(II) exempts any public official in the conduct of his or her official duties from the 'real estate broker' definition.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(III), which group of persons acting under proper authorization is exempt from the 'real estate broker' definition?
choice_a: Any receiver, trustee, administrator, conservator, executor, or guardian
choice_b: Any licensed mortgage loan originator
choice_c: Any property management franchise owner
choice_d: Any escrow agent employed by a title company
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(III) exempts any receiver, trustee, administrator, conservator, executor, or guardian acting under proper authorization from the 'real estate broker' definition.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(IV), a person or firm acting personally (or a corporation acting through its officers or regularly salaried employees) is exempt from the 'real estate broker' definition when:
choice_a: Selling real estate it owns to the general public through open marketing
choice_b: Acquiring or negotiating to acquire any interest in real estate on its own behalf as principal
choice_c: Managing rental property it owns for a management fee
choice_d: Listing a shopping center it owns with a licensed broker
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(IV) exempts a person, firm, LLC, or association acting personally, or a corporation acting through officers or regularly salaried employees, on its own behalf as principal in acquiring or negotiating to acquire any interest in real estate.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(VI), the 'real estate broker' definition exempts persons engaged in negotiating or dealing in which specialized category of interests?
choice_a: Water rights adjudicated under Colorado's prior appropriation system
choice_b: Timeshare interests in resort condominiums
choice_c: Oil, gas, or other mineral leases or severed mineral/royalty interests, including related pipeline rights-of-way and easements
choice_d: Agricultural conservation easements
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(VI) exempts persons or entities negotiating, acquiring, selling, leasing, or dealing in oil, gas, or other mineral leases or severed mineral or royalty interests, including related easements, rights-of-way, and pipeline facilities.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(XII), which employee is exempt from the 'real estate broker' definition?
choice_a: A commission-only leasing agent working for multiple unrelated apartment owners
choice_b: A regularly salaried employee who manages condominium units for an HOA under a management contract
choice_c: A part-time leasing consultant paid per signed lease
choice_d: A regularly salaried employee of an owner of an apartment building or complex who acts as an on-site manager of that building or complex
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(XII) exempts a regularly salaried employee of an owner of an apartment building or complex who acts as an on-site manager of that building or complex.

question: Under § 12-10-201(6)(b)(XV), a sole proprietor, corporation, partnership, or LLC selling Colorado property is exempt from the 'real estate broker' definition, acting through its officers, partners, or regularly salaried employees, when the transaction involves:
choice_a: A purchaser who is in the business of developing land for residential, commercial, or industrial purposes
choice_b: A purchaser who intends to occupy the property as a primary residence
choice_c: A purchaser who is a licensed real estate broker
choice_d: A sale price under $100,000
explanation: Section 12-10-201(6)(b)(XV) exempts a seller acting through officers, partners, or regularly salaried employees where the purchaser of the property is in the business of developing land for residential, commercial, or industrial purposes.

question: Under § 12-10-402, for purposes of part 4 (Brokerage Relationships), the term 'Broker' is defined by:
choice_a: A wholly independent definition unrelated to part 2's licensing definition
choice_b: Cross-reference to the definition of 'real estate broker' in section 12-10-201(6), except as modified in part 4
choice_c: Reference only to brokers holding an Employing Broker level license
choice_d: Reference only to brokers who have designated themselves as single agents
explanation: Section 12-10-402 defines 'Broker' by reference to the definition in section 12-10-201(6), except as that meaning is modified within part 4 itself.

question: Under § 12-10-402, a 'Customer' is defined as:
choice_a: Any member of the public who contacts a broker for information
choice_b: A party represented by a broker as a single agent
choice_c: A party to a real estate transaction with whom the broker has no brokerage relationship because the party has not engaged or employed a broker
choice_d: A party who has signed a buyer-agency agreement
explanation: Section 12-10-402 defines 'Customer' as a party to a real estate transaction with whom the broker has no brokerage relationship because that party has not engaged or employed a broker.

question: Under § 12-10-402, a 'Designated Broker' is:
choice_a: The single broker who owns a majority interest in a brokerage firm
choice_b: Any broker who has completed the state examination but not the national examination
choice_c: A broker appointed by the real estate commission to investigate a firm
choice_d: An employing or employed broker designated in writing by an employing broker to serve as a single agent or transaction-broker for a seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant
explanation: Section 12-10-402 defines 'Designated Broker' as an employing or employed broker designated in writing by an employing broker to serve as a single agent or transaction-broker for a seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant; the definition excludes single-person brokerage firms.

question: Under § 12-10-402, a 'Dual Agent' is defined as a broker who:
choice_a: With the written informed consent of all parties to a contemplated transaction, is engaged as a limited agent for both the seller and buyer, or both the landlord and tenant
choice_b: Represents a buyer in one transaction and a seller in a separate, unrelated transaction
choice_c: Works for two different brokerage firms simultaneously
choice_d: Is licensed in both Colorado and a neighboring state
explanation: Section 12-10-402 defines 'Dual Agent' as a broker who, with the written informed consent of all parties to a contemplated real estate transaction, is engaged as a limited agent for both the seller and buyer or both the landlord and tenant.
source_note: hedge: sourced from a current secondary-source mirror of Colo. Rev. Stat. § 12-10-402, not independently confirmed against the official leg.colorado.gov PDF text

question: Under § 12-10-402, a 'Limited Agent' is an agent whose duties are restricted to:
choice_a: Only the ministerial acts assigned by the employing broker
choice_b: Those set out in sections 12-10-404 and 12-10-405, plus any additional duties agreed upon under section 12-10-403(5)
choice_c: Duties owed exclusively to the party paying the commission
choice_d: Duties that automatically expire at closing
explanation: Section 12-10-402 defines 'Limited Agent' as an agent whose duties are restricted to those in sections 12-10-404 and 12-10-405, in addition to any duties agreed to under section 12-10-403(5).

question: Under § 12-10-402, a 'Single Agent' is a broker who:
choice_a: Is the only licensed broker at a one-person brokerage firm
choice_b: Represents both parties without disclosure
choice_c: Represents only one party in a transaction, including a buyer's agent, seller's agent, landlord's agent, or tenant's agent
choice_d: Has not yet been designated by an employing broker
explanation: Section 12-10-402 defines 'Single Agent' as a broker representing only one party in a real estate transaction, encompassing buyer's agents, seller's agents, landlord's agents, and tenant's agents.

question: Under § 12-10-402, a 'Subagent' is:
choice_a: An unlicensed assistant who performs clerical tasks for a broker
choice_b: A broker who works exclusively with a single client for a flat fee
choice_c: Any broker employed by the same firm as the listing broker
choice_d: A broker engaged to act for another broker in performing brokerage tasks for a principal, owing the principal the same obligations and responsibilities as the principal's own broker
explanation: Section 12-10-402 defines 'Subagent' as a broker engaged to act for another broker in performing brokerage tasks for a principal, and states that the subagent owes the same obligations and responsibilities to the principal as the principal's own broker does.

question: Under § 12-10-402, a 'Transaction-Broker' is a broker who:
choice_a: Assists the parties to a transaction with communication, negotiation, and the closing process without being an agent or advocate for the interests of any party
choice_b: Represents only the seller but discloses material facts to the buyer
choice_c: Is engaged by both parties as a limited agent with written informed consent
choice_d: Acts as an unlicensed facilitator exempt from part 2 licensing
explanation: Section 12-10-402 defines 'Transaction-Broker' as a broker who assists the parties to a transaction with communication, negotiation, and the closing of the transaction, without being an agent or advocate for the interests of any party to the transaction.

question: Broker Nguyen assists a buyer and a seller with communication, drafting, negotiation, and closing, but by written agreement is not acting as an advocate for either party's interests. Under § 12-10-402, Nguyen is best classified as a:
choice_a: Single agent
choice_b: Transaction-broker
choice_c: Dual agent
choice_d: Subagent
explanation: This describes the statutory definition of 'Transaction-Broker' in § 12-10-402: a broker who assists parties with communication, negotiation, and closing without being an agent or advocate for any party's interests, as distinguished from a single agent (who represents one party) or dual agent (who represents both as a limited agent).

question: Broker Alvarez is engaged by Broker Chen to help perform brokerage tasks for Chen's seller-client, and owes the seller the same obligations Chen owes. Under § 12-10-402, Alvarez's role is that of a:
choice_a: Transaction-broker
choice_b: Customer
choice_c: Subagent
choice_d: Designated broker
explanation: Section 12-10-402 defines 'Subagent' as a broker engaged to act for another broker in performing brokerage tasks for a principal, owing that principal the same obligations and responsibilities as the principal's own broker.

question: Under § 12-10-403(2), absent a written agreement establishing a single agency relationship, a broker engaged in a real estate transaction is, by default, considered a:
choice_a: Dual agent
choice_b: Subagent
choice_c: Customer's representative
choice_d: Transaction-broker
explanation: Section 12-10-403(2) provides that a broker shall be considered a transaction-broker unless a single agency relationship is established through a written agreement between the broker and the party or parties to be represented.

question: Under § 12-10-403(3), a single broker may work with the same party under different brokerage relationships across different transactions -- for example, acting as a seller's agent when listing that party's home, and as a:
choice_a: Transaction-broker or buyer's agent when helping the same party buy a different property
choice_b: Dual agent automatically in every subsequent transaction with that party
choice_c: Subagent only, regardless of the new transaction's terms
choice_d: Customer, since a prior client relationship bars any new agency
explanation: Section 12-10-403(3) allows a broker to work with a single party in separate transactions under different relationships -- for instance, selling one property as a seller's agent and later working with that same seller, as a buyer, in a transaction-broker or buyer's agent capacity -- provided the broker complies with part 4 in establishing each relationship.

question: Under § 12-10-403(6)(a), when a real estate brokerage firm has more than one licensed natural person, who must be designated to work with a seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant as a designated broker?
choice_a: Only the employing broker personally, in every transaction
choice_b: The employing broker or an individual broker employed or engaged by that employing broker
choice_c: Any licensee chosen at random by the firm's office manager
choice_d: A broker approved in advance by the real estate commission for that specific transaction
explanation: Section 12-10-403(6)(a) requires that in a multi-licensee firm, the employing broker or an individual broker employed or engaged by that employing broker be designated as the designated broker, and permits the employing broker to designate more than one individual broker for the same seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant.

question: Under § 12-10-403(6)(b), the brokerage relationship, duties, and obligations established between a client and a designated broker:
choice_a: Automatically extend to every broker employed by the same firm
choice_b: Extend to the employing broker only, but not to the firm itself
choice_c: Do not extend to the employing broker, to any other non-designated broker at the firm, or to the entity that employs the broker
choice_d: Extend to the firm's parent company if the firm is a franchise
explanation: Section 12-10-403(6)(b) states that the brokerage relationship established with a designated broker, including its duties, obligations, and responsibilities, does not extend to the employing broker, to any other broker employed or engaged by that employing broker who was not so designated, or to the firm, partnership, LLC, association, corporation, or other entity that employs the broker.

question: A brokerage firm designates Broker A as single agent for the seller and Broker B (a different broker at the same firm) as single agent for the buyer in the same transaction. Under § 12-10-403(6)(c), this arrangement:
choice_a: Automatically creates dual agency for the employing broker
choice_b: Is prohibited outright under Colorado law
choice_c: Requires the real estate commission's prior written approval
choice_d: Does not create dual agency for the employing broker or the firm
explanation: Section 12-10-403(6)(c) permits a real estate broker to have designated brokers working as single agents for opposite sides of the same transaction without creating dual agency for the employing broker or any other broker employed or engaged by that employing broker.

question: Under § 12-10-403(6)(d), an individual broker designated to work with both the seller/landlord and the buyer/tenant in the same transaction may serve as a transaction-broker for both, or as a single agent for one side treating the other as a customer, but may NOT serve as:
choice_a: A single agent for both sides of the same transaction
choice_b: A transaction-broker for either side individually
choice_c: A designated broker at all in that transaction
choice_d: A subagent for the listing broker
explanation: Section 12-10-403(6)(d) permits an individual designated broker to work for both sides as a transaction-broker for both, or as a single agent for one side treating the other as a customer, but expressly prohibits acting as a single agent for both sides of the same transaction.

question: Under § 12-10-403(6)(f), when a designated broker serves as a single agent under section 12-10-404 or 12-10-405, what is the effect on the employing or other employed broker who was not designated?
choice_a: The non-designated broker is automatically deemed to share the designated broker's fiduciary duties
choice_b: There is no imputation of knowledge to the non-designated employing or employed broker
choice_c: The non-designated broker becomes personally liable for the designated broker's representations
choice_d: The non-designated broker must co-sign all transaction documents
explanation: Section 12-10-403(6)(f) provides that when a designated broker serves as a single agent, there is no imputation of knowledge to the employing or employed broker who was not so designated.

question: Under § 12-10-403(7), a seller, buyer, landlord, or tenant is vicariously liable for a broker's acts or omissions only if those acts or omissions were:
choice_a: Committed within the broker's normal course of business, regardless of client involvement
choice_b: Covered by the broker's errors-and-omissions insurance
choice_c: Approved, directed, or ratified by the seller, buyer, landlord, or tenant
choice_d: Performed by a designated broker rather than an associate broker
explanation: Section 12-10-403(7) states that no seller, buyer, landlord, or tenant shall be vicariously liable for a broker's acts or omissions that have not been approved, directed, or ratified by that seller, buyer, landlord, or tenant -- a protection echoed in the part 4 legislative declaration at § 12-10-401(1).

question: Under § 12-10-401(2), the express statutory purpose of enacting part 4 of article 10 is to:
choice_a: Establish minimum continuing education requirements for licensees
choice_b: Create the trust account recordkeeping requirements applicable to all brokers
choice_c: Set the fee schedule for real estate broker license renewal
choice_d: Govern the relationships between real estate brokers and sellers, landlords, buyers, and tenants in real estate transactions
explanation: Section 12-10-401(2) states that part 4 is enacted to govern the relationships between real estate brokers and sellers, landlords, buyers, and tenants in real estate transactions.

question: Section 12-10-402 still defines 'Dual Agent' as a broker acting as a limited agent for both sides with written informed consent, yet under § 12-10-406 a broker:
choice_a: Shall not establish dual agency with any seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant
choice_b: May establish dual agency only with the real estate commission's prior written approval
choice_c: May establish dual agency freely, since § 12-10-406 merely restates the § 12-10-402 definition
choice_d: May establish dual agency only in commercial transactions
explanation: Although 'Dual Agent' remains a defined term in § 12-10-402, current § 12-10-406 flatly prohibits a broker from establishing dual agency with any seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant -- the definition is retained for statutory completeness even though the underlying relationship it describes may no longer be lawfully created.
